subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The four factors of production are land, labour, capital and:
questions.explain: Enterprise (entrepreneurship) combines land, labour and capital to produce goods and services.

questions.q: A business in the tertiary sector primarily:
questions.explain: The tertiary sector provides services; primary extracts, secondary manufactures, quaternary is knowledge/R&D.

questions.q: Businesses create value by:
options: Transforming inputs into more valuable outputs
questions.explain: Adding value means outputs are worth more than the cost of the inputs used.

questions.q: Limited liability means owners:
options: Can only lose the amount they invested
Are liable for all business debts personally
questions.explain: With limited liability, personal assets are protected beyond the amount invested.

questions.q: A sole trader has:
questions.explain: Sole traders are personally liable for all business debts (unlimited liability).

questions.q: A publicly held company (plc) is able to:
options: Sell shares to the general public
Only be owned by one person
questions.explain: A plc can sell shares to the public via a stock exchange; a private (Ltd) company cannot.

questions.q: A cooperative is owned and operated:
options: By its members for their mutual benefit
questions.explain: Cooperatives are member-owned organisations run for members' shared benefit.

questions.q: A mission statement sets out an organisation's:
questions.explain: The mission states the business's fundamental purpose; the vision states its long-term aspiration.

questions.q: In SMART objectives, the 'T' stands for:
questions.explain: SMART = Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound.

questions.q: 'Increase market share by 5% within 12 months' is best described as a:
questions.explain: It is specific, measurable, time-bound and so on — a SMART objective.

questions.q: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) means a business:
options: Acts ethically toward society and the environment
questions.explain: CSR is acting in the interests of society and the environment beyond legal minimums.

questions.q: Which is an internal stakeholder?
questions.explain: Internal stakeholders (employees, managers, owners) are inside the business; customers/suppliers/community are external.

questions.q: Shareholders wanting higher dividends while employees want higher pay is an example of:
questions.explain: Different stakeholders have competing interests, creating stakeholder conflict.

questions.q: Economies of scale occur when:
options: Average costs fall as output rises
Average costs rise as output rises
questions.explain: Growing output can lower unit (average) costs — economies of scale.

questions.q: A merger is when:
options: Two firms agree to combine into one
One firm buys another against its wishes
A firm opens a new branch
questions.explain: A merger is a mutually agreed combination; a hostile takeover is against the target's wishes.

questions.q: A restaurant chain grows by opening more of its own outlets. This is:
questions.explain: Expanding using the firm's own resources is internal/organic growth.

questions.q: External growth includes mergers, acquisitions and:
questions.explain: External growth involves combining with or acquiring other firms (mergers, acquisitions, takeovers, JVs, franchising).

questions.q: A multinational company (MNC) is one that:
options: Produces or operates in more than one country
questions.explain: MNCs have operations/production in multiple countries.

questions.q: A benefit an MNC can bring to a host country is:
questions.explain: MNCs can create jobs, bring investment and transfer skills/technology to host countries.

questions.q: A potential drawback of MNCs for a host country is:
options: Profits may be repatriated and local firms out-competed
questions.explain: Concerns include profit repatriation, harm to local competitors and environmental/social impacts.

specSource: IB Diploma Business Management guide (first assessment 2024); Unit 1 — Introduction to business management
